lines: Every good Popkin ends. Here is the send-off.
On the Popkin home, the Host opens Popkin settings, and chooses Wrap up: End it now and send the recap.
The wrap-up screen asks: Wrap up Lakeside Weekend? It says what happens next for all fourteen of you: everyone gets a recap, and chat goes quiet.
Keep the photo album is on. Turn it off, and photos are removed after thirty days.
Choose Wrap it up. The button reads Wrapping up, and the recap opens for everyone who has the Popkin open.
This Popkin wrapped up. What a time.
Fourteen people showed up. One thousand two hundred and eighty-six messages sent, forty-eight photos shared, and the top-rated moment: Sunrise canoe to Heron Point.
Save the album prepares a zip of every photo, and shows its progress: Preparing twelve of forty-eight.
If the album was not kept, a notice counts the days: Photos go in twelve days.
The chat stays readable: This Popkin has wrapped up. Messages stay, but nobody can post new ones.
Photos and Experiences stay readable too, and nothing can be added.
A Popkin with an end date warns in its last hour: One hour left.
Every member sees the banner. The Host's offers Change.
When the time comes, it wraps up by itself, with its photo album kept.
From the recap, the Host can Pop up another with this crew. A member can Start your own Popkin.

lines.text: On a phone, the recap is one column.
From ten twenty-four pixels, its pictures sit beside its numbers and actions.
And from seven sixty-eight, the wrap-up screen shows the recap it will make.

lines: What no screen shows: once a Popkin has wrapped up, every request to add to it is refused, and only the Host can wrap one up.
Still to come: Change how long it lasts.
That is journey nine. Popkin is a free platform for pop-up communities.
